claim: Apple's HealthKit splits time in bed into awake, core, deep and REM sleep samples.
quote: These detailed samples show when the user was awake, in core sleep, in deep sleep, or in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep.

claim: In HealthKit, in-bed time and the sleep-state samples are separate samples that overlap.
quote: To track both the amount of time a person spends in bed and the quality and quantity of their sleep, use samples with overlapping times.

claim: Apple Watch records awake samples only between two sleep samples.
quote: Samples recorded by Apple Watch only include awake samples that occur between two sleep samples.

claim: Health Connect has a stage for sleep whose stage is not known.
quote: The user is asleep but the particular stage of sleep (light, deep or REM) is unknown.

claim: Health Connect separates awake in bed from out of bed.
quote: The user is out of bed and assumed to be awake.

claim: Health Connect has an awake-in-bed stage.
quote: The user is awake and in bed.

claim: Health Connect has an unknown stage.
quote: Use this type if the stage of sleep is unknown.

claim: Google Health API's classic sleep has three stage types: awake, restless and asleep.
quote: Classic sleep is a sleep with 3 stages types: AWAKE, RESTLESS and ASLEEP.

claim: Google Health API's staged sleep overwrites the classic stages with awake, light, REM and deep.
quote: an additional processing pass can calculate stages more precisely, overwriting the prior stages with AWAKE, LIGHT, REM and DEEP.

claim: Google Health API does not compute stages for a sleep shorter than three hours.
quote: Sleep stages cannot be computed because the sleep log is a nap (has < 3h duration).

claim: Fitbit's staged logs return deep, light, REM and wake at 30-second granularity.
quote: Levels data is returned with 30-second granularity. 'Sleep Stages' levels include deep, light, rem, and wake.

claim: Fitbit's classic logs return asleep, restless and awake at 60-second granularity.
quote: Levels data returned with 60-second granularity. 'Sleep Pattern' levels include asleep, restless, and awake.

claim: Fitbit dates a sleep log by the day it ends.
quote: The dateOfSleep in the GET sleep log endpoint response is the date on which the sleep event ends.

claim: Oura reports deep sleep duration in seconds.
quote: Duration spent in deep sleep in seconds.

claim: Oura reports light sleep duration in seconds.
quote: Duration spent in light sleep in seconds.

claim: Oura reports REM sleep duration in seconds.
quote: Duration spent in REM sleep in seconds.

claim: Oura reports awake time in seconds.
quote: Duration spent awake in seconds.

claim: Oura publishes a stage timeline at 5-minute resolution.
quote: 5-minute sleep phase classification for the period where every character corresponds to:

claim: Oura publishes a stage timeline at 30-second resolution.
quote: 30-second sleep phase classification for the period where every character corresponds to:

claim: WHOOP reports light sleep as a total in milliseconds.
quote: Total time the user spent in light sleep, in milliseconds

claim: WHOOP calls deep sleep Slow Wave Sleep.
quote: Total time the user spent in Slow Wave Sleep (SWS), in milliseconds

claim: WHOOP reports REM sleep as a total in milliseconds.
quote: Total time the user spent in Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep, in milliseconds

claim: WHOOP reports awake time as a total in milliseconds.
quote: Total time the user spent awake, in milliseconds

claim: WHOOP reports time with no data separately.
quote: Total time WHOOP did not receive data from the user during the sleep, in milliseconds

claim: Garmin's public Health API page lists sleep among its metrics without naming sleep stages.
quote: Steps Intensity Minutes Sleep Calories Heart Rate Stress Pulse Ox Body Battery Body Composition Respiration Blood Pressure

claim: HealthKit groups its sleep-state values (awake, asleepCore, asleepDeep, asleepREM, asleepUnspecified) apart from in-bed time.
quote: Values for Tracking Sleep States

claim: HealthKit has an asleepUnspecified value.
quote: HKCategoryValueSleepAnalysis/asleepUnspecified

claim: HealthKit has an asleepCore value.
quote: HKCategoryValueSleepAnalysis/asleepCore

claim: HealthKit tracks in-bed time with its own value.
quote: Values for Tracking Time In-Bed

claim: HealthKit lists the plain asleep value as deprecated.
quote: Deprecated values
